before:
Saint Vincent and the Grenadines' first international airport, at Argyle about 8 km from the capital Kingstown, and the country's main gateway.

It is what made long haul access possible. The airport connects directly to Atlanta, Miami, John F. Kennedy, Toronto and London Heathrow as well as other Caribbean airports.

It is also the hub for island hopping. Several airlines run an extensive network of domestic flights from Argyle to every destination in the Grenadines, and it is the primary hub for SVG Air and Mustique Airways, who together operate 17 aircraft through an alliance with bases in St Vincent, Antigua and Grenada.

It is the largest of five airports in the country. The others are J. F. Mitchell Airport on Bequia, Canouan, Mustique and Union Island, all in the Grenadines.

It is the second solar powered airport in the Caribbean after V. C. Bird International in Antigua.

It is often called Argyle Airport or simply AIA.
after:
Saint Vincent and the Grenadines' main airport, at Argyle on mainland St Vincent, about 8 km from the capital, Kingstown.

Virgin Atlantic flies from London Heathrow three times a week, and says the flight touches down in Barbados for about an hour, with passengers staying on board. The country's tourism authority also lists direct flights, some of them seasonal, from Atlanta, Miami, New York JFK and Toronto. Regional airlines link it with other Caribbean islands.

Two local airlines, SVG Air and Mustique Airways, fly on from here to the Grenadines.

It is the largest of the country's five airports. The other four are on Bequia (J F Mitchell Airport), Canouan, Mustique and Union Island.

It is often called AIA.

claims.claim: Virgin Atlantic flies from London Heathrow three times a week
claims.inAfter: Virgin Atlantic flies from London Heathrow three times a week
claims.note: Was 'connects directly to ... London Heathrow'. The airline and the tourism authority agree on three flights a week (Wednesday, Friday and Sunday). The flight is not non-stop (next claim). The UK CAA's 2025 route table, which still files St Vincent under the old airport name E T JOSHUA, has only 148 passengers between Heathrow and St Vincent in 2025 (1,196 in 2024), against 482,348 between Heathrow and Bridgetown. That fits passengers on a through flight being counted against Barbados, the first stop, though the table does not say so; its St Vincent figure is therefore not used as a measure of this route.

claims.claim: the tourism authority lists direct flights, some seasonal, from Atlanta, Miami, New York JFK and Toronto
claims.inAfter: The country's tourism authority also lists direct flights, some of them seasonal, from Atlanta, Miami, New York JFK and Toronto.
claims.note: The four cities are in both sources; the seasons are the tourism authority's alone, so the sentence is attributed to it. Delta flies from Atlanta on Saturdays in January to August and December; American flies from Miami all year (daily October to April, five a week May to September) and from New York JFK on Saturdays December to March; Caribbean Airlines and JetBlue fly from JFK twice a week each; Air Canada Rouge flies from Toronto all year. The authority also lists American from Charlotte, Saturdays December to March, which the old text did not have (held back, below). The airport's own airline page shows airline logos only, with no text to quote.

claims.claim: the country's first international airport
claims.wasBefore: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines' first international airport
claims.why: Wikipedia alone. The operator's own history says only that in 2005 the government decided 'to build a new international airport at Argyle', and the tourism authority calls it 'the newest international airport in the Eastern Caribbean'; neither says first. The code SVD belonged to the old E T Joshua Airport at Arnos Vale (OurAirports), now closed. Replaced by 'main airport', which two sources support.

claims.claim: it is what made long haul access possible
claims.wasBefore: It is what made long haul access possible.
claims.why: A judgement no source makes in those words. The operator's history says E T Joshua's development was 'severely constrained, both in terms of the width and length of the runway' and that Argyle's runway was designed for 'jets as large as the Boeing 747-400s'; Wikipedia says the airport was 'expected to' attract direct flights from Canada, the US and the UK. The text now names the long haul flights instead.

claims.claim: connects directly to Atlanta, Miami, John F. Kennedy, Toronto and London Heathrow, and other Caribbean airports
claims.wasBefore: The airport connects directly to Atlanta, Miami, John F. Kennedy, Toronto and London Heathrow as well as other Caribbean airports.
claims.why: Rewritten, not dropped. The Heathrow flight is not non-stop: Virgin Atlantic's own page says it touches down in Barbados for about an hour. The four North American cities are kept, attributed to the tourism authority with its note that some flights are seasonal, and the Caribbean links are kept as regional flights.

claims.claim: the hub for island hopping
claims.wasBefore: It is also the hub for island hopping.
claims.why: Overstated. Wikipedia calls it 'a major gateway to the Grenadines', but SVG Air, which flies to Bequia, Canouan and Union Island, tells visitors on its own home page that 'The Easiest Way to Get to the Grenadines is via Barbados', and Mustique Airways sells a 'Shared Charter from Barbados'. The flights from here to the Grenadines are kept.

sources.quote: The Easiest Way to Get to the Grenadines is via Barbados
Shared Charter from Barbados

claims.claim: several airlines, an extensive network to every destination in the Grenadines
claims.wasBefore: Several airlines run an extensive network of domestic flights from Argyle to every destination in the Grenadines
claims.why: 'Every destination' overstates it: besides Argyle only Bequia, Canouan, Mustique and Union Island have airports (OurAirports). The tourism authority's matching sentence shares Wikipedia's wording, so it is not a second source. Softened to the two local airlines that fly from here to the Grenadines.

claims.claim: the primary hub for SVG Air and Mustique Airways
claims.wasBefore: it is the primary hub for SVG Air and Mustique Airways
claims.why: 'Primary hub' rests on Wikipedia alone. SVG Air's own pages give bases in St Vincent and the Grenadines, Grenada and Carriacou, and Antigua and Barbuda, with no address at the airport; Mustique Airways gives its address as Argyle International Airport. Softened to 'two local airlines ... fly on from here'.

claims.claim: 17 aircraft through an alliance with bases in St Vincent, Antigua and Grenada
claims.wasBefore: who together operate 17 aircraft through an alliance with bases in St Vincent, Antigua and Grenada
claims.why: Contradicted by SVG Air's own page, which says it operates 7 aircraft with bases in St Vincent and the Grenadines, Grenada and Carriacou, and Antigua and Barbuda; neither airline's site mentions an alliance. A fleet count is of no use to an agent, so it is not replaced.

sources.quote: we have grown to now operate 7 aircraft throughout the Caribbean with bases in St. Vincent and the Grenadines, Grenada and Carriacou and Antigua and Barbuda

claims.claim: all in the Grenadines
claims.why: Not wrong, but the only second source that places the four airports in the Grenadines is the tourism authority's introduction, which shares Wikipedia's wording. The islands are named instead, and the airlines' Grenadines flights are kept.

claims.claim: the second solar powered airport in the Caribbean after V. C. Bird International
claims.wasBefore: It is the second solar powered airport in the Caribbean after V. C. Bird International in Antigua.
claims.why: One source. The tourism authority's page carries Wikipedia's sentence word for word ('The airport is the second solar powered airport in the Caribbean, following V. C. Bird International Airport in Antigua'), so the two count once, and no independent source was found.

claims.claim: also called Argyle Airport
claims.wasBefore: It is often called Argyle Airport or simply AIA.
claims.why: 'Argyle Airport' rests on Wikipedia alone; the operator and the tourism authority use 'Argyle International Airport' and 'AIA'. The sentence is kept as 'It is often called AIA.'

claims.claim: the old airport's name and code (E T Joshua, SVD)
claims.why: Held back: a new fact, for Andy. Argyle replaced E T Joshua Airport at Arnos Vale on 14 February 2017 (Wikipedia) and took over its code, SVD (OurAirports lists E T Joshua as closed, with SVD among its other names). The UK CAA's 2025 route table still files St Vincent's traffic under 'E T JOSHUA' (2025, 148 passengers from Heathrow), so the old name may still turn up in some systems. A line such as 'It replaced E T Joshua Airport in 2017 and took over its code' would help an agent who meets the old name.
